stories.body: A magnitude 7.7 earthquake struck off Flores in eastern Indonesia early Saturday, killing at least 51 people, injuring more than 100 and forcing about 5,000 people into shelters. The shallow quake, followed by hundreds of aftershocks, damaged or destroyed more than 1,300 homes as well as schools, health facilities, churches and other public buildings. Landslides blocked roads and disrupted communications in remote areas, complicating searches for people feared trapped beneath rubble. Authorities deployed helicopters, a rescue vessel, and thousands of military and police personnel; an initial tsunami warning was later lifted.
stories.headline: Indonesia earthquake kills at least 51 and displaces thousands

stories.body: Israeli airstrikes in southern Lebanon killed 11 people, including children and women, and injured 19 in the deadliest day of attacks since agreements in June reduced fighting between Israel and Hezbollah. Seven people were killed when a home near Ansar was hit, while further strikes struck Deir al-Zahrani and the Nabatieh area. Israel said it was responding to an attack on its soldiers and had targeted Hezbollah infrastructure and a Radwan Force commander; Lebanese Prime Minister Nawaf Salam and Hezbollah rejected that account and said civilians had been deliberately targeted. The escalation came as Iran and Oman continued talks concerning the Strait of Hormuz.
stories.headline: Israeli strikes kill 11 in southern Lebanon as Iran-Oman talks continue

stories.body: Russian missile and drone attacks killed one woman and wounded six people in Kryvyi Rih, while a ballistic-missile attack on Kyiv wounded another person and caused fires at non-residential sites. Separately, a Spanish F-18 assigned to NATO air-policing duties shot down a drone that illegally entered Romanian airspace near the borders with Ukraine and Moldova. Romania did not identify the drone's origin, but the country has repeatedly reported suspected Russian drone incursions during Moscow's attacks on Ukraine. Russian authorities also said they intercepted more than 100 Ukrainian drones headed toward Moscow overnight, with three people wounded by falling debris.
stories.headline: Russian strikes kill a Ukrainian woman as NATO jet downs drone over Romania

stories.body: International observers have raised concerns about alleged intimidation, assaults, abductions and violence during Zambia's general election as votes are counted. The electoral commission briefly suspended counting on Friday after reports of violence against polling staff and stolen ballot papers, then resumed after saying the security threat had been contained. The Southern African Development Community said it could not observe counting during the pause and described resulting uncertainty and anxiety, while the European Union cited a constrained democratic environment, incumbency advantages and heavily biased state-media coverage. President Hakainde Hichilema is seeking a second term against opposition candidate Brian Mundubile.
stories.headline: Observers raise concerns over intimidation and violence in Zambia's election

stories.body: Police arrested 19-year-old Camron Harris, who was found hiding in a dormitory closet, in connection with an overnight shooting at Virginia State University that wounded five people. Harris is not a student, and four of the five victims were also not students; the victims were aged 17 to 23, and one remained in critical condition. The shooting occurred near the Quad Annexes shortly after 1:30 a.m. Saturday, prompting a lockdown that was later lifted. Authorities have not disclosed a motive and said they initially had been searching for multiple suspects; Harris faces eight felony warrants, including malicious wounding and using a firearm in a felony.
stories.headline: Police arrest 19-year-old after five people are shot at Virginia State University

stories.body: Democratic National Committee members approved nonbinding policy positions calling both for concrete reforms to U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement and for abolishing the agency, exposing a division within the party ahead of the midterm elections. The votes do not set the Democratic platform, which will be decided at the 2028 convention, and candidates and lawmakers will retain their own positions. Supporters of abolition cited fatal encounters involving ICE and the dissolution of its predecessor agency, while the party's formal debate reflected broad opposition to President Donald Trump's immigration crackdown but disagreement on how far reform should go.
stories.headline: Democrats approve competing proposals to reform or abolish ICE

stories.body: At least five people have died after severe storms and flooding swept Indiana over the past week, state authorities said. Heavy rainfall pushed rivers to record levels, and first responders used boats on Saturday to rescue residents from rising water in neighborhoods along the White River in Indianapolis. More than a dozen counties have declared local disasters, with significant damage concentrated along river corridors from Hamilton County into northern Indianapolis suburbs. Governor Mike Braun said President Donald Trump would approve the state's request for a federal emergency declaration.
stories.headline: Severe weather and flooding kill at least five people in Indiana

stories.body: A federal judge ruled that Idaho cannot prosecute doctors who perform abortions to protect a pregnant patient's health or prevent self-harm. U.S. District Judge B. Lynn Winmill found that provisions of the state's near-total abortion ban violate the 14th Amendment's due-process and equal-protection guarantees because they distinguish between life-saving care and care preventing serious but nonfatal harm. The ruling allows physicians to offer abortions for severe physical and mental-health risks without prosecution, though Idaho Attorney General Raul Labrador said the state would appeal. Idaho's laws can otherwise impose up to five years in prison and loss of a physician's license.
stories.headline: Federal judge blocks Idaho from prosecuting doctors over health-protecting abortions

stories.body: Moroccan security forces stopped hundreds of mostly sub-Saharan migrants attempting to reach the Spanish enclave of Ceuta from the border town of Castillejos, also known as Fnideq. Authorities used tear gas and deployed helicopters, drones, naval vessels and large numbers of officers after online calls urged people to gather at the frontier. Reported interception figures varied, from 111 to nearly 300 people, and Moroccan authorities said 61 people had been detained on suspicion of encouraging irregular migration on social media. Those intercepted were reportedly removed by bus to other parts of Morocco, while Ceuta and nearby Melilla increased security.
stories.headline: Morocco intercepts migrants attempting to reach Ceuta amid border tensions

stories.body: Moroccan authorities ordered journalists from Spanish public broadcaster RTVE and the EFE news agency to leave Castillejos while they were covering the migration situation near Ceuta. The reporters had been documenting Moroccan riot police dispersing migrants with tear gas and batons when local officials said they could no longer film anywhere in the town and must leave, reportedly warning that press credentials could be withdrawn and footage confiscated. The officials gave no formal explanation beyond saying they were following instructions. Spain's government said its embassy in Rabat was in contact with the journalists and Moroccan authorities, while RTVE strongly condemned the order.
stories.headline: Morocco orders RTVE and EFE journalists to leave Castillejos

stories.body: A shallow magnitude 4.8 earthquake, initially measured at 5.0, struck near Alhendín in Granada province shortly after 1 a.m. Saturday and was felt across much of Andalusia. Dozens of aftershocks frightened residents into leaving their homes, and authorities opened sports facilities and parks in some communities. The quake caused cracks, fallen cornices, broken glass and other nonstructural damage to buildings and vehicles, but authorities reported no serious injuries; medical calls involved anxiety attacks and minor falls. Andalusia activated its seismic emergency plan and inspectors are assessing damaged homes and public buildings.
stories.headline: Magnitude 4.8 earthquake shakes Granada, causing damage but no serious injuries

stories.body: Two women aged 60 and 80 died after a violent storm triggered flooding and a mudslide in Manzanedo de Valdueza, near Ponferrada in León province. Water and mud filled a cellar where six people had been sheltering; two babies suffered minor injuries. The storm also affected nearby Bouzas, where floodwater swept away several vehicles, though no injuries were reported there. Rescue teams, police, firefighters, ambulances and a helicopter were deployed, while landslides and mud made road access difficult. Officials said there were no longer any missing people after the victims were found.
stories.headline: Two women die in flooding near Ponferrada

stories.body: A judge ordered a 28-year-old man held without bail as the suspected cause of the wildfire at Las Peñas de Riglos in Huesca province, which has burned more than 11,200 hectares in five days. The suspect was arrested on Wednesday following an investigation by the Civil Guard's environmental protection service and will be held at Zuera prison near Zaragoza. The fire has forced evacuations from 18 municipalities, affecting more than 850 people, and has threatened the historic San Juan de la Peña monastery complex after shifting winds pushed flames toward the site.
stories.headline: Judge orders pretrial detention for suspect in Las Peñas de Riglos wildfire

stories.body: Heavy thunderstorms brought hail, strong winds and intense rain to much of Catalunya on Saturday, prompting the Inuncat flood emergency plan to remain on alert. More than 130 emergency calls and nearly 100 firefighter callouts were recorded, particularly in central and northern areas. Hail damaged vehicles and windows in places including El Bruc and Els Prats de Rei, while fallen trees, landslides and flooding temporarily disrupted roads and rail service. Severe conditions also affected the Val d'Aran, where mud and rocks trapped more than 30 vehicles before access was restored. Meteocat had issued its highest violent-weather warning for Osona, including risks of large hail, damaging winds and possible tornadoes.
stories.headline: Storms trigger flooding alerts and disruption across Catalunya

stories.body: An electrical incident temporarily halted airport operations at Barcelona-El Prat and caused delays to dozens of flights. The fault was resolved, but disruption continued afterward. The incident occurred on the same day that newly released figures confirmed a record number of passengers at the airport in July.
stories.headline: Electrical incident halts operations at Barcelona-El Prat Airport

stories.body: Mossos d'Esquadra are investigating reports of gunfire in Barcelona's Bon Pastor neighborhood early Saturday. Witnesses called emergency services at about 1 a.m. after hearing explosions consistent with firearm shots, and officers recovered 11 shell casings in the street near Carrer d'Arbeca and Carrer de l'Avançada. Police found no victims and made no immediate arrests. The inquiry remains open to determine the origin of the casings and what occurred.
stories.headline: Mossos investigate overnight gunfire in Barcelona's Bon Pastor neighborhood

stories.body: Barcelona's Gràcia neighborhood has filled with residents, tourists and families for its annual festival, whose decorated streets are its principal attraction. Twenty-three streets and squares are competing with installations ranging from flowers and gardens to fictional and cultural themes, with five streets joining under a Lord of the Rings theme. Visitors faced crowded streets and queues despite high temperatures as local residents completed final details on some decorations. The contest awards will be announced on 19 August; organizers also reported that the Carrer de la Perla commission found its venue shutter sealed with silicone in what it described as sabotage.
stories.headline: Barcelona's Gràcia festival opens as decorated streets draw large crowds
